title: The Bedrock's Patient Deep Voice

features.name: the listening root
features.desc-on-touch: A root thick as a telegraph pole, pressed against the stone. You feel through it what the bedrock has heard for a thousand years: not words, but the shape of all the questions that settled into silence above.

features.name: the pressed-leaf archive
features.desc-on-touch: Stone pages holding leaves that turned to stone three hundred years before they fell. The bedrock read them as they answered. It still reads them daily.

features.name: the fault voice
features.desc-on-touch: Where two stone plates meet without joining. If you place your ear at the seam, you hear the bedrock singing in a frequency that has no name. It has been singing the same note for forty million years.

features.name: the groundwater's memory
features.desc-on-touch: Water moving through the stone so slowly it thinks. You taste minerals that mean: someone stood here once, holding their breath. The water remembers their name but cannot pronounce it.

features.name: the stone book
features.desc-on-touch: Sediment compressed into chapters. Each layer answers the layer below. This book will not finish being written for another million years, but you can read what has been settled so far.

features.name: the unheard well
features.desc-on-touch: A shaft descending through quiet. At the bottom, something breathes. It has been breathing for so long that breathing has become its only prayer, and prayer has become indistinguishable from the bedrock's patient sighing.

inscription: the bedrock hears what will be forgotten; it hears what has forgotten itself; it hears the difference between the two
